      "observations": [
        "All 316 owned diff lines across four paths were inspected, including the entire 183-line new test and fake-server hook. At final chunk handling, the new condition requires chunked mode, a non-header download, a positive expected total and origin plus current literal size below that total. It aborts instead of normal finalization. Both branches still reach the common UID bookkeeping reset; a bare early return would skip that work.",
        "The selected parser consumer treats a response literal whose count differs from the requested fetch size as the last chunk. The added guard compares that raw literal count plus origin with the expected message total. A truncated literal that already stops parsing follows the existing abort path. The code does not repair every false RFC822.SIZE report, nonchunked short response or network failure.",
        "The actual abort chain invokes the folder write sink. With an offline header it calls EndNewOfflineMessage(NS_ERROR_ABORT); that failure branch clears the Offline flag and asks the message store to discard a pending stream. Success finalizes the store token and sets Offline. These are source contracts, not measured disk integrity or a completed re-download.",
        "The fake server parses partial offsets/counts as integers, then clips only chunked BODY[] responses at _truncateBodyAt and advertises the resulting literal length. The ASCII test keeps the true message size, uses 4,000-byte chunks with a 2,000-byte threshold and a 20,000-byte truncation point, and suppresses stream/URL promise rejections before checking flags. Its four assertions all have nonempty expected-behavior messages; missing “should” alone is not reported as a defect in this authored patch. No test asserts returned error status, saved body bytes, discarded file contents, attachment completeness or a later re-fetch.",
        "The exact previously read PromiseUrlListener, PromiseRequestObserver and PromiseStreamListener objects from 5644 are reused unchanged with their original timestamps. Their non-NS_OK paths reject promises. The test comment saying streams/URLs may “resolve with an error” therefore describes rejection imprecisely; the actual catch calls intentionally ignore those rejections and leave the Offline assertions as the result check. No new promise convention follows.",
